subject: Post-call exec recap: Parkview Health — business outcomes, procurement path, next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <treynolds@parkviewhealth.com>, Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@parkviewhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call exec recap: Parkview Health — business outcomes, procurement path, next steps

Tom / Sofia — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick executive recap and agreed next steps so we have alignment for your leadership and procurement teams.

Summary of today's discussion (15 min exec + 30 min technical):
- Business outcomes: reduce average time-to-resolution for patient inquiry routing by ~40%, lower manual triage costs in urgent-care flow, and standardize discharge-note summarization for care coordination.
- Key pain points: inconsistent triage rules across clinics, high latency on current on-prem NLP pipeline during peak hours, and manual QA burden on clinical staff.
- Success metrics you care about: 40% reduction in triage time, 20% decrease in manual QA hours, sub-300ms 95th percentile latency for short-form inference.

Risks / blockers we flagged:
- Data residency & PHI handling (need clarity on which data fields will be sent to hosted endpoints vs private deployment).
- Procurement path: Parkview indicated an initial vendor evaluation with procurement + legal followed by a 2–6 week onboarding window (dependent on SOC2 evidence and vendor onboarding policy).
- Integration: EHR connector and HL7 message mapping will need a 2-week engineering spike to estimate full effort.

Proposed short-term scope (demo -> pilot):
1) POC (4 weeks): Hosted endpoint + private VPC option for PHI-sensitive routes. Pilot includes 3 clinics, triage model, and discharge-note summarization.
2) Deliverables: SOW, SOC2 Type II evidence, sample integration plan, and a 1-page runbook for escalation and rollback.

Next steps (owners & timelines):
- Marissa (Redwood): share draft SOW and cost estimate by EOD tomorrow. [Attachment: SOW-draft-parkview-v1.docx]
- Tom (Parkview): share procurement contact and any onboarding questionnaires by Fri 3/19.
- Sofia (Parkview): confirm list of PHI fields and desired data residency for pilot by 3/22.
- Laura (Redwood Legal/PS): advise on any contract redlines and standard indemnity language — target internal review by 3/20.

Escalation items for leadership: potential SLA exceptions for initial pilot due to custom connector work; if procurement requires an on-prem-only deployment, timeline will shift by 6–8 weeks.

If useful, we can schedule a 30-minute leadership sync (Tom + Sofia + Parkview procurement rep + Laura) early next week to walk the SOW and procurement checklist.

Thanks again — we felt strong alignment on outcomes and can move fast once procurement confirms the path.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0132
Redwood Inference

Marissa — appreciate the clear recap and the SOW. Quick notes from our side: we are aligned on the outcomes and pilot scope.

Procurement contact: procurement@parkviewhealth.com (cc'd in this thread). They will need the SOW and SOC2 evidence; they typically run vendor security questionnaires and run a vendor risk review (~2–4 weeks if all evidence is available).

Thanks Marissa — looping in legal and PS for visibility. A few internal items to track:

1) SOW comments: will review and push back on any broad indemnity or data-use sections. Expect a first-pass redline by Fri 3/19.
2) Security evidence: Parkview is asking for SOC2 Type II and a short architecture diagram showing data flows for PHI. We can supply SOC2 report and a sanitized architecture diagram (no customer data) — need to confirm whether Parkview will accept Redwood's hosted SOC2 or requires on-prem evidence.
3) Procurement path & timeline: based on our experience, once procurement has complete documentation, vendor onboarding + legal review takes ~3–6 weeks. If they insist on on-prem, that will add procurement and infra lead times.

Action items:
- Laura (Legal): share redlines by 3/19.
- Sean (PS): please start a high-level integration estimate (HL7/EHR connector) and note any questions for Parkview engineering. Target to have estimate by 3/22.

I'll also draft a one-page risk & mitigation memo for Marissa to share with Parkview leadership if we need to accelerate approvals.
